B. Walk backward while looking continuously through the viewfinder to frame a wider angle near ledges or moving traffic.

D. Climb over safety guardrails at scenic overlooks so foreground fences do not appear in the frame.

pamphlet_excerpts: International Standards Organization Acronym: ISO is simply an acronym for the International Standards Organization (p. 22).
Sensor Light Sensitivity Standards: This organization sets the standard by which camera sensors and their sensitivity to light are measured (p. 22).
Electronic Sensor Sensitivity Control: By changing the ISO setting, you control the relative sensitivity of the electronics in your camera to light (p. 22).
Doubling ISO Sensitivity Values: With every doubling of the number, the camera's digital sensor becomes twice as sensitive to the light available for the picture (p. 22).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Adjust Electronic Sensor Sensitivity: By changing the ISO setting, you control the relative sensitivity of the electronics in your camera to light (p. 22).
Step 2 - Double the ISO Number: With every doubling of the number, the camera's digital sensor becomes twice as sensitive to the light available for the picture (p. 22).

patrol_quiz_bank.question: While composing photographs outdoors near a canyon rim, roadway, or approaching thunderstorm, what safety rule takes priority over capturing the shot?
options: A. Maintain situational awareness of your footing and surroundings before stepping while looking through the viewfinder, and seek shelter immediately if lightning or severe weather approaches.
B. Walk backward while looking continuously through the viewfinder to frame a wider angle near ledges or moving traffic.
C. Hold a carbon-fiber tripod high overhead in an open field during a thunderstorm to keep the camera dry.
D. Climb over safety guardrails at scenic overlooks so foreground fences do not appear in the frame.
choices: A. Maintain situational awareness of your footing and surroundings before stepping while looking through the viewfinder, and seek shelter immediately if lightning or severe weather approaches.
B. Walk backward while looking continuously through the viewfinder to frame a wider angle near ledges or moving traffic.
C. Hold a carbon-fiber tripod high overhead in an open field during a thunderstorm to keep the camera dry.
D. Climb over safety guardrails at scenic overlooks so foreground fences do not appear in the frame.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Maintain situational awareness of your footing and surroundings before stepping while looking through the viewfinder, and seek shelter immediately if lightning or severe weather approaches.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Photographers frequently get injured when stepping backward or sideways while focused on a viewfinder or LCD screen; always check footing and surroundings before moving, and never use tripods as lightning rods in storms.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: How does changing your camera's ISO from 200 to 800 affect the digital sensor?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: How does changing your camera's ISO from 200 to 800 affect the digital sensor?
options: A. It makes the sensor half as sensitive to light and narrows the angle of view
B. It makes the sensor four times as sensitive to available light because sensitivity doubles each time the ISO number doubles
C. It physically opens the lens aperture four stops wider to create a shallower depth of field
D. It slows the shutter speed by four seconds to blur moving water in bright sunlight
choices: A. It makes the sensor half as sensitive to light and narrows the angle of view
B. It makes the sensor four times as sensitive to available light because sensitivity doubles each time the ISO number doubles
C. It physically opens the lens aperture four stops wider to create a shallower depth of field
D. It slows the shutter speed by four seconds to blur moving water in bright sunlight
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. It makes the sensor four times as sensitive to available light because sensitivity doubles each time the ISO number doubles
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Every time you double the ISO number (from 200 to 400, and from 400 to 800), the digital sensor becomes twice as sensitive to light, making 800 four times as sensitive as 200 (p. 22).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: What happens inside a camera to create an exposure when you press the shutter button?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: What happens inside a camera to create an exposure when you press the shutter button?
options: A. The memory card projects a beam of light through the viewfinder onto the subject
B. The LCD screen flashes internally to print the image onto the glass lens element
C. Light reflecting off the subject passes through the lens and aperture while the shutter opens briefly to expose the image sensor
D. The battery permanently locks the aperture closed so no light can reach the sensor
choices: A. The memory card projects a beam of light through the viewfinder onto the subject
B. The LCD screen flashes internally to print the image onto the glass lens element
C. Light reflecting off the subject passes through the lens and aperture while the shutter opens briefly to expose the image sensor
D. The battery permanently locks the aperture closed so no light can reach the sensor
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Light reflecting off the subject passes through the lens and aperture while the shutter opens briefly to expose the image sensor
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): A camera is a light-tight box where reflected light from the subject enters through the lens and aperture while the shutter opens for a set duration, allowing the sensor to record the image (p. 39).
